title: Stabilize build provenance inputs
description:
Make ordinary validation and test builds insensitive to Git metadata-only changes and the wall clock while preserving an explicit, reproducible provenance interface for releases. The version command must continue to report injected release metadata accurately.

## Background

The package build script watches `.git/index`, `HEAD`, and refs and embeds the current time. Staging or committing unchanged Rust sources can therefore rerun the build script and relink every package test target.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Ordinary test and validation builds do not use `.git/index`, branch refs, or the current wall clock as changing compiler inputs, and two builds from identical source and explicit environment produce identical build provenance values.
- [hard] REQ-02: After an initial `cargo test --workspace --no-run --message-format=json` build, both staging a metadata-only file change and creating a metadata-only commit followed by the same command produce zero non-fresh Rust test compiler artifacts when Rust sources and explicit provenance environment variables are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Release builds accept `JIT_BUILD_GIT_HASH`, `JIT_BUILD_GIT_SHORT_HASH`, `JIT_BUILD_GIT_DIRTY`, and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` as authoritative injected inputs, and `jit version --json` reports those exact supplied values.
- [hard] REQ-04: Repeating a release build with the same injected commit fields and source-date epoch produces identical reported provenance, while changing an injected value invalidates the affected build output.
- [hard] REQ-05: Builds without Git metadata still succeed and report stable documented fallback values rather than a wall-clock-dependent timestamp.
- [hard] REQ-06: Regression coverage exercises the metadata-only invalidation contract in an isolated temporary Git repository and preserves the existing clean, dirty, and no-Git version-reporting contracts.
